ⓘ How to Read This Report

Compliance Status

Compliant  — no open issues and all waivers are active.
Conditionally Compliant  — no open or invalid issues, but one or more waivers are not yet active.
Non-Compliant  — has open issues (Analyze / Fix Planned) or invalid / missing / mismatched waivers.

Waiver Quality

A waivered issue is one whose KW status is Ignore, Defer, or Not a Problem. Waiver quality is determined by the waiver ID in the issue comment.

  • Open Issues and Invalid / Missing / Mismatched Waivers1 — contribute to Non-Compliant; rows highlighted red in the Raw Issues table.
  • Inactive Waivers2 — contribute to Conditionally Compliant; rows highlighted yellow in the Raw Issues table.
  • Active Waivers — waiver status is Deviation Active; no row highlighting (fully compliant).

1 Invalid = missing or invalid waiver ID   Mismatch = waiver checker code does not match the KW issue checker code
2 Inactive = waiver found but not yet active

Klocwork Query

The Klocwork Query field in the Configuration Summary shows the filter used to fetch issues from the Klocwork server. Klocwork queries follow a simple convention:

  • * — Wildcard: fetch all issues in the project with no filter applied.
  • +module:name — Include only issues belonging to the module named name. Multiple +module: terms narrow the scope to those modules only.
  • -module:name — Exclude issues belonging to the module named name from the results. Commonly used to skip test code, third-party libraries, or example projects that are not under the project's direct quality control.

Example: * -module:test -module:examples fetches all issues except those in the test and examples modules.

ISS-1290JIRAR.11.4: MISRA.CAST.OBJ_PTR_TO_INT.2012Deviation ActiveMISRA CPermittedCode Quality (Portability)ProjectUse Case 1: Overlay structures are used to access IP MMRs. Pointers of such types must be initialized with appropriate addresses to be able to access the MMRs. An example is mentioned below: struct CC_PRIVID_REG reg = GET_CC_PRIVID_REG(offset);   Use Case 2: A lot of TI SoCs feature address busses wider than 32 bits. On such SoCs, 32 bit cores use a RAT to map region of external memory space to an internal address range. Sometimes local addresses must be converted to global ones for variety of reasons (like programming the global address in some MMR.) ret = socmem_to_global((local_phys_addr_t)&sa2ul_sec_ctx_mem00,                    &sa2ul_ctx_st.sec_ctx_mem_phys); Use Case 3: Conversions between pointers and integers are required for the purpose of calling functions or initializing structures. len = get_sec_ap_dlen((u32) &SEC_AP_REGS.rx_ctrl); Use Case 4: Overlay structures are used to access structured data. Pointers of such types must be initialized with appropriate addresses to be able to access the data. An example is mentioned below: struct rom_firmware_data rom_data = (struct rom_firmware_data ) ROM_FW_DATA_LOC; Use Case 5: Conversions between pointers and integers are required for the purpose of data transfer. u8 rand_str = (u8 ) (bin_addr + bcfg_size - TI_X509_ENC_EXT_RS_LEN); Use Case 6: Addresses of some standard registers must be stored in pointer variables to access those addresses. addr = SYST_CVR;

ISS-1697JIRACXX.ID_VIS.GLOBAL_VARIABLE.EXTERNDeviation ActiveMISRA CPermittedCode Quality (Portability)ProjectCXX.ID_VIS.GLOBAL_VARIABLE.EXTERNConclusion: The wide visibility of gReadbackVissRxTprdMem is a deliberate and necessary design decision to ensure correct DDR-backed, cache-line aligned memory allocation for UDMA TR descriptor memory, as mandated by the MPU configuration. PDK-18821JIRANUM.OVERFLOW.DF: Possible numeric overflow or wraparoundDeviation ActiveMISRA CPermittedNA - Tool IssueProjectThe reported arithmetic expressions may theoretically overflow; however, all involved variables are strictly bounded and validated during system initialization. The operational ranges ensure that subtraction, increment, and multiplication remain within valid limits. No wraparound can occur in any execution path. Adding explicit overflow checks would unnecessarily impact performance and reduce code readability without improving functional safety. (Case ID: 01509909)
